svg.title: Split-Half FP32 RoPE — AVX2 Vector Path with Scalar Reference
svg.desc: Technical infographic of ck_rope_split_f32_avx2 and ck_rope_split_f32_reference: split-half input pairing, eight-pair AVX2 lane mapping, cosine/sine loads, four multiplies followed by add/subtract, in-place safety (all loads before any store), scalar tail, validation path, and the no-allocation workspace contract.
svg.text: Split-Half FP32 RoPE — AVX2 Vector Path with Scalar Reference
ck_rope_split_f32_avx2 / ck_rope_split_f32_reference · dst[i] = a·c − b·s · dst[i+half] = b·c + a·s

g.text: checked identically in the reference and AVX2 paths
pair i uses c[i], s[i]: dst[i] = a·c − b·s
• No malloc, no temp / workspace buffer.
4 · AVX2 Lane Mapping — 8 pairs per iteration
one 256-bit lane per half → 8 pairs processed per iteration
5 · Dataflow — Four Multiplies, Then Add / Subtract
No FMA contraction (−ffp-contract=off): same op order as reference → bitwise-identical results
6 · In-Place Safety — All Loads Before Any Store
dst == src is safe: all four 256-bit vectors (a, b, c, s)
are loaded before any _mm256_storeu_ps writes dst.
Scalar tail keeps the same load-then-store order.
src / dst — same buffer (dst == src supported)
runs only when half % 8 ≠ 0 (i left over from AVX2 loop)
Same four multiplies, then add/subtract — identical numerical order
to the AVX2 path (no FMA contraction) → bitwise-identical results.
